videos.subtitle_summary:

An image of a person resembling former South Korean President Park Chung-hee (who ordered the suppression of the May 18 Gwangju Democratization Movement) holding a Starbucks cup has been circulating online, sparking concerns about insensitive marketing and potential second-degree harm to victims' families.
2. The controversy has escalated into an ideological conflict, with Starbucks being perceived as symbolizing conservative forces. Worry is growing that irresponsible content production could lead to further harm towards the 518 Gwangju Democratization Movement victims and their families.
3. The situation could potentially worsen for Starbucks Corporation, as concerns about brand value damage have led to speculation about a possible contract termination by IMART, which owns 17.5% of Starbucks Korea. This could result in financial loss and the need to transfer shares back to IMART. The importance of brand value is emphasized in this situation.

videos.title: Samsung Electronics to pay special bonuses in company stock... concerns over 'overhang'? / Korea ...
videos.subtitle_summary: Samsung Electronics will pay a special bonus of 31 trillion won in company stock this year. The bonus shares will be issued from existing shares and not newly issued shares. The bonus is guaranteed for 10 years, with approximately 10.5% of the annual operating profit being used for it. The remaining Samsung Electronics shares are now 1.846 million common shares after a share buyback worth 14.58 trillion won in February. One-third of the bonus shares can be sold immediately, while the rest can be sold after one and two years. There is concern that this could increase the company's supply in the market, but it is expected to have minimal impact due to the large daily trading volume of Samsung Electronics and the fact that the bonus shares will be issued over three years. The main burden on Samsung Electronics is expected to come from the rising semiconductor prices overwhelming the increased income.
